investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-15T20:49–20:56Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence at all — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient allocatable capacity for that resource, and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption was also ruled out (no victims found on the 2 eligible nodes; preemption unhelpful on the 4 ineligible nodes). The pod remained in Unschedulable state for ~123–147 seconds across all three checks, causing the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) to time out before any VM was assigned, so zero evidence was written and the expected-output contract was fully violated.

investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a credit_balance_exhausted error. The server translated this into a generation_error SSE frame (evidence: failed-check.evidence), which terminated the stream before a generation_completed frame or image URL could be emitted. Both required contract assertions — frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true — were therefore violated (evidence: expected-output.contract, failed-check.message). This is an eval infrastructure / external dependency failure; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the packet.

investigations.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a credit_balance_exhausted error. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, and no image URL artifact was produced, causing both contract assertions to fail.

When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1977-1985), the upstream OpenAI API responded with error type "insufficient_quota" and code "credit_balance_exhausted". The server translated this into a generation_error SSE frame (evidence: failed-check.evidence), which terminated the stream before a generation_completed frame or image URL could be emitted. Both required contract assertions — frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true — were therefore violated (evidence: expected-output.contract, failed-check.message). This is an eval infrastructure / external dependency failure; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the packet.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returns 502/424 provider_account_unavailable
investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval failed because exactly one of two configured models, aura-gpt-5-5, returned a 502 bad-gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable. The other model, aura-claude-sonnet-4-6, passed cleanly. This is a localized eval failure against the aura-gpt-5-5 runtime path; no sibling checks failed and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.
investigations.rootCause: AURA's backend was temporarily unable to reach the upstream model provider for aura-gpt-5-5 at the time of the eval run (2026-08-15T20:48:59Z). The runtime endpoint POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502 containing a nested 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." This caused the model-matrix check to record allPassed=false and failedModelCount=1, violating the expected-output contract assertions that require allPassed=true and failedModelCount=0. The failure is isolated to the aura-gpt-5-5 model slot; the eval infrastructure itself, the eval runner, and the Anthropic-backed model all functioned correctly.

failed-check.evidence: results[0] for aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 shows ok=true, provider=anthropic, messageSample='hello from aura', confirming the eval runner and harness path are functional.
expected-output.contract: assertions require allPassed=true and failedModelCount=0 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 333-334); both are violated by the aura-gpt-5-5 result.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=12039, well within the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold (source.check-config.model-matrix), ruling out a timeout as the proximate cause.
source.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1936: runner iterates over args.models, meaning each model is tested independently; the failure is scoped to the aura-gpt-5-5 iteration only.
possibleCauses: Most likely: Transient upstream provider unavailability for the OpenAI/GPT-5 provider at the time of the eval run, as explicitly stated in the 424 error message and provider_account_unavailable code (failed-check.evidence).

Less likely but possible: A persistent or recurring degradation of the provider account or API key configuration on AURA's side for the aura-gpt-5-5 model, which would produce repeated failures across runs.

Less likely: A misconfiguration or routing issue introduced to the aura-gpt-5-5 model slot in the runtime harness that causes provider resolution to fail (provider=null, resolvedModel=null in the evidence), which could be independent of upstream availability.
Least likely given no sibling failures: A shared infrastructure issue affecting only the GPT-family provider integration layer within AURA's backend, not the Anthropic integration.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-15T20:49–20:56Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence at all — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient allocatable capacity for that resource, and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption was also ruled out (no victims found on the 2 eligible nodes; preemption unhelpful on the 4 ineligible nodes). The pod remained in Unschedulable state for ~123–147 seconds across all three checks, causing the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) to time out before any VM was assigned, so zero evidence was written and the expected-output contract was fully violated.

investigations.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 499 minutes old at the time of the run (2026-08-15T20:56:41.868Z), which exceeds the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the snapshot freshness assertion alone.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot is structurally valid and sourced from github-actions (hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true, unknownFeatureCount=0), but its age of 499 minutes violates the snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300 assertion defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482. This is an eval-detected staleness condition scoped to the snapshot publication pipeline; no evidence of a user-facing outage or broader site disruption is present.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 499' — the single violated assertion in the contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482).

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=499, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true, unknownFeatureCount=0 — confirms the snapshot exists and is structurally valid but is stale.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } is the earliest and only violated contract boundary (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482).

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed with HTTP 200 responses — confirms the public website itself is reachable and the failure is isolated to snapshot freshness.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check is registered as required=false, statusImpact='informational', staleAfterMinutes=360 — the registry staleAfterMinutes (360) is more permissive than the contract max (300), indicating a potential misalignment between registry config and the expected-output contract assertion.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=76 — the eval probe itself completed normally; the failure is in the data value, not in probe execution or network reachability.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot did not execute or did not complete successfully within the last 300 minutes, leaving the previously published snapshot (499 minutes old) in place at the snapshotUrl.

Secondary: The workflow ran but failed to publish the updated snapshot to https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json (e.g., a GitHub Pages deployment step failed, a permissions error, or a push was skipped), so the stale file persisted.

Secondary: The workflow schedule was changed, disabled, or skipped (e.g., due to a branch protection rule, a workflow file change, or GitHub Actions queue delays), causing the publication cadence to exceed 300 minutes.

Lower likelihood: A misconfiguration mismatch — the registry entry in infra/evals/status/features.json sets staleAfterMinutes=360 while the expected-output contract in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json enforces max=300 — could cause the eval to fail even when the workflow ran within the registry's intended tolerance window. If the workflow ran ~301–360 minutes ago, the snapshot would be considered fresh by the registry but stale by the contract.
